doc: The complete worked review, definitions/designers/examples/certificate-expiry.md, read through post-incident-review.fbl#markdown (FBL 0.7, sections 4.8, 5.2, 5.3 and 15.3), LF endings. Line 1 is the envelope, the binding's required header. Line 2 is the mark line, a statement the rule marks (no within) matches; the specification maps Marks as the document (DESL 5.2), so it gives the document's lastEntry, lastFactor and lastAction. The items under Summary and Impact are matched by rules whose types Summary and Impact the specification maps as the document too: they give timeZone, summary, affected, effect and duration and no element. The title, the paragraph under it and the legend under How to read this file, whose fenced block holds three items in the line forms and no element (4.8 rule 8), are unbound and kept. Every entry, factor, action and category is listed in the order of the file: E-0009 stands last although its time, 00:12, is the third earliest, since a reading keeps the file's order and the order of the Timeline part is the designer's (spec User Story 1, scenario 2; DESL 7.8.2). Times are as written, with their offsets (DESL 4.2, timezone preserve); a milestone is stated by its enumeration key, so `mitigation start` reads mitigationStart (DESL 4.4); an ordinary entry has no kind. Word slots with many are stated as JSON arrays in order, and a single word slot without a word is not named (FBL 4.6). An action's checkbox reads through the map to a bool; F-0005, rejected, is read and kept, with its reason as its detail. A category's id is derived, 'category/' and its name in lower case.
